props.title: One from the Heart
props.initialSlug: A love story with a heart.

sections.content: One from the Heart represents Francis Ford Coppola's bold experimental musical, shot entirely on soundstages at his Zoetrope Studios. Coming after Apocalypse Now (1979), Coppola bet everything on this neon-drenched Las Vegas romance, using groundbreaking video pre-visualization techniques and spending millions on elaborate sets. The film's commercial failure bankrupted Zoetrope, but its visual influence echoes through works like Lost in Translation (2003) and Drive (2011). Vittorio Storaro's cinematography creates a dreamlike artificial world that perfectly captures Vegas unreality.

movies.title: All That Jazz
movies.slug: Fosse's experimental musical about show business excess

sections.content: The film's innovative use of Tom Waits and Crystal Gayle's soundtrack creates a melancholic counterpoint to the artificial glamour. This technique of using singer-songwriter material as emotional commentary influenced later films like Magnolia (1999) and Inside Llewyn Davis (2013). The story follows Frannie and Hank, a working-class couple whose fantasy versions of themselves clash with reality during one long Vegas night.

Coppola's decision to shoot entirely on soundstages marks a crucial moment in 1980s cinema's return to artificiality, predating the similar approaches of Dick Tracy (1990) and Streets of Fire (1984). The film's commercial failure pushed Hollywood away from such ambitious experimental musicals until Moulin Rouge! (2001) revived the form two decades later. movies.title: The Cotton Club
movies.slug: Coppola's next film, mixing music and drama in stylized sets

sections.content: The film's use of video previsualization - recording rehearsals on video to plan complex shots - revolutionized production planning. While the movie lost millions, this technique became industry standard, used in everything from Avatar (2009) to La La Land (2016). The elaborate soundstage production, with its computer-controlled lighting system, presaged today's LED volume technology used in The Mandalorian (2019).
